title: Eliminating Repeated Recursive Calls in largest2 with let
description: Use let to bind the recursive result (largest2 (cdr L)) once so both the comparison and the else branch reuse it.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Lines 1-4 define `largest2` with the same one-element base case: when `(null? (cdr L))` is true on line 3, line 4 returns `(car L)`.

On line 5, `(let ((largestval (largest2 (cdr L)))) ...)` evaluates `(largest2 (cdr L))` once and binds the returned number to `largestval`. Lines 6-8 then test `(>= (car L) largestval)` and return either `(car L)` or `largestval`.
Compare lines 5-8 with `largest`: binding `largestval` on line 5 means each recursive step calls `largest2` on `(cdr L)` exactly once, whether `(>= (car L) largestval)` is `#t` or `#f`.

steps.question: When `(largest2 (list 1 2 4 3))` runs on line 10, how many total calls to `largest2` are made across the 4-element list, and what value is returned?
steps.answer: Each element triggers at most one recursive call on `(cdr L)`. `largest2` is called 4 times in total: `'(1 2 4 3)`, `'(2 4 3)`, `'(4 3)`, and `'(3)`. It returns `4`.
